doc.title: Herb Ellis interviewed by Michael Woods, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Meeting Oscar Peterson in Buffalo and joining his trio
summary: A trio formed from Jimmy Dorsey band members played a Buffalo hotel, where Peterson sat in; four years later he asked Ellis to join.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Good, good. Tell us how you got started working with probably one of the greatest trios in all of jazz — Oscar Peterson and Ray Brown.

I was playing, I had been with bands, I’d been with Jimmy Dorsey, and the three of us in Jimmy Dorsey’s band, the bassist and the pianist and myself formed a trio, sort of a la Nat Cole, and we were playing in Buffalo. And we played in the same hotel for, oh months at a time. And the people from Canada, there was no liquor in Canada on Sundays at that time, but they’d come over for the music. And a lot of them came. And one night they brought Oscar Peterson with them. And he sat in and played with us and then after the job Oscar and I went out and we played in a different place. And from that meeting and playing together, about four years later, when he needed a guitarist for his group, he asked for me. And I was not that well known. He could have had anybody he wanted, but thank God he chose me.
